Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: one additional view of the EXACT SAME closed ritual treasure chest for a 2D isometric mobile game.
Input1 is the accepted closed chest, the authoritative object design, colours, shapes and camera elevation. Turn the OBJECT by a quarter turn on the ground, keeping the CAMERA fixed. This is the EAST-facing view: its opening/front points toward SCREEN LOWER-RIGHT.
The broad front panel with the violet pointed lock MUST now be the RIGHT visible face: it runs diagonally from the central bottom corner UP toward the right-hand corner, slope -0.5. The short side is the LEFT visible face, slope +0.5. This swap of the long and short visible faces is essential. See the top, the long front on RIGHT, the short side on LEFT. Do not return the input front-on-left view.
Retain the same squat rectangular body (long width:depth about1.4:1), slate charcoal claw-like ribs, two small swept horn tips, dark plum boards, one large recessed violet seal, CLOSED lid, thin violet inner seam. Do not redesign any fitting. Redraw lighting for fixed SCREEN UPPER-LEFT illumination; do not simply mirror the bitmap. Broad painted shading, navy contour, softened chunky bevels, readable at96px wide.
Orthographic 2:1 dimetric projection: upright verticals, parallel ground diagonals slopes +/-0.5, no convergence or camera tilt. Entire grounded object centred with generous margins. No pedestal.
Native-alpha TRANSPARENT backdrop, no surrounding haze, outer glow, cast shadow, ground, text or checkerboard. Violet contained in the lock/seam. One complete solid opaque chest only.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Create the REAR THREE-QUARTER VIEW of this exact CLOSED ritual chest for a 2D isometric game.
Input1 is object/style reference. Turn the chest180 degrees on the ground while keeping the same camera. The chest FRONT and its violet lock now point AWAY from us, toward screen UPPER-RIGHT (logical north). We see the broad BACK panel on the LEFT visible face, its edges sloping +0.5, and the SHORT side on the RIGHT, edges -0.5.
IMPORTANT: the violet pointed FRONT LOCK is completely HIDDEN on the opposite side. The near broad panel is the BACK: show TWO simple substantial dark iron HINGES at the lid/body joint on this near back panel. No keyhole, jewel, front clasp, decorative face or invented second lock on the back. Keep the same plum timber and slate charcoal ribs; quiet plain back boards. Same two swept horn tips, now seen from behind. CLOSED lid.
Preserve the exact family of body proportions, low rectangular chest1.4width:1depth, chunky softened bevels, navy contours and broad painted shading. Maintain fixed upper-left SCREEN lighting; do not mirror the reference. Orthographic2:1 dimetric ground axes +/-.5, verticals upright. Top, wide BACK on left, short side on right; never return a front view. Rear identification comes from the hinge pair and absence of front seal. Only faint violet seam under closed lid.
One complete solid sprite centred with generous transparent margins. Native-alpha TRANSPARENT background, no aura, haze, floor, cast shadow, text or checkerboard. No redesign or extra ornaments.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Input1 is the edit target, an OPEN isometric ritual chest. Input2 is its exact CLOSED state and authoritative lock design.
Correct ONLY the front lock hardware on input1: replace the plain rectangular plate with two rivets with the SAME pointed slate metal escutcheon, violet diamond/hexagonal border and dark key slot seen on input2. The fixed lower lock escutcheon stays attached to the FRONT BODY below the rim, in precisely its original visual place; it does NOT disappear when unlocked. The small upper pointed catch belongs to the raised lid, separated from the fixed keyhole plate by the existing opening. Make the violet inset softly luminous, slightly less intense while unlocked, still recognisably the identical mechanism. Never put a second lock on a side.
Keep input1's OPEN lid, current pile of SMALL coins, body, horns, proportions, exact camera angle, shadows, framing and all other details. Front is the broad LEFT visible face facing screen lower-left. Native-alpha transparent background. No ground, shadow, glow outside object, text or extra ornaments. This must look like one and the same chest changing state, not a new model. Orthographic2:1 ground axes, vertical uprights. Do not enlarge the coins.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Clean this exact game sprite. Remove the stray pale gray smudge in the upper-right transparent margin completely: all space outside the chest must be fully transparent native alpha, no haze or residue. Also remove the tiny violet triangle on the underside of the raised lid: that upper catch should be plain charcoal iron. Keep the SINGLE violet lock with keyhole firmly attached to the lower front body, exactly as it is. Everything else including small coins, body, lid angle, horns, lighting, composition and colours remains unchanged. One isolated open chest on transparent background. ERASE the entire doubled V/arrow/chevron shaped ornament on the lid. Replace that central lid edge with a SINGLE STRAIGHT simple beveled metal lip continuing the broad slate band. Keep the separate violet pointed keyhole lock on the LOWER BODY EXACTLY as is. Keep the whole chest silhouette, horns, raised lid position, camera, small gold coins, plum wood, slate colours, body and lighting unchanged. True transparent native-alpha background; no stray pixels, haze, cast shadow, floor, text. One chest, one decorative lock on the lower body, simple straight lip on top.
